def is_inside(path: str) -> bool:
    """True when path, read relative to the base directory, stays inside it.

    Rejects absolute paths and any path whose ".." components climb above
    the base. Paths that wander and come back (sub/../a.txt) are accepted.
    """
    pre path.byte_len() < 4096
    ex is_inside("a.txt") == True
    ex is_inside("sub/../a.txt") == True
    ex is_inside("../x") == False
    ex is_inside("sub/../../x") == False
    ex is_inside("/etc/passwd") == False
    if path.startswith("/"):
        return False
    depth = 0
    for part in path.split("/"):
        if part == "" or part == ".":
            continue
        if part == "..":
            if depth == 0:
                return False
            depth -= 1
        else:
            depth += 1
    return True

def read_public(path: str) -> str uses fs:
    """Return the text of path inside the directory notes, or "".

    Missing, unreadable, or escaping paths give an empty string. Only files
    inside notes are read; the function narrows fs to notes before reading.
    Examples are omitted here because calling this function needs the fs
    capability, which an ex line cannot provide.
    """
    pre path.byte_len() < 4096
    post is_inside(path) or out == ""
    if not is_inside(path):
        return ""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        text = fs.read(path) else ""
        return text
